name: Brownish Pink
lede: Brownish Pink is a modifier on [[pink]], a phrase Paterson's dictionary reaches for to describe other named colors rather than one he enters on its own.

sections.title: A phrase borrowed to define other words
sections.body:
As a swatch name, Brownish Pink is recorded only by the xkcd 2010 crowd survey [1]. But Paterson's *A Dictionary of Colour* already uses the phrase twice: he calls "nude" a brownish pink, quoting a 1900 *Times* reference to "nude-coloured chiffon dresses" [2]. He also notes that tea rose, usually a yellowish pink, is "sometimes a brownish pink," and cites Fowler's *English Usage* for the first recorded use of "tea rose" as a color term in 1892 [2].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[old-rose|Old Rose]], only 2.6 units away and read as almost the same color [3]. [[old-rose|Dirty Pink]] sits a little further out, redder by comparison [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color appears in 119 of our 23,781 paintings, about 0.5 percent, rarer than 55 percent of our named colors, as photographed [4]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, 3.2 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive, and Henri Matisse is its most devoted painter here, with 4 of his 50 works carrying it, 6.8 times his baseline [4]. The earliest match dates to the year 1000, 1,010 years before the xkcd survey; our archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [4].
